blocks.text: Setting up your Mac for evaluation work

Google Sheets does not have a native Mac application. You should use Google Chrome for the most stable experience. To make it feel like a real app, open your sheet in Chrome. Click the three-dot menu at the top right. Select Cast, Save, and Share, then choose Install page as app. This creates a shortcut in your Applications folder that opens Sheets in its own window. You can keep this window open on your Mac alongside your evaluation portal.
Essential shortcuts for search engine evaluators

Speed is vital when you are tracking hundreds of tasks. Learning keyboard shortcuts saves you from constant mouse movement. Press ⌘ + / to see every available shortcut in the app. Use ⌘ + ⇧ + H for quick find and replace when you need to update project IDs or feedback codes. Use ⌘ + ⌥ + 9 to hide rows you have already completed.

items: Use ⌘ + ⌥ + 0 to hide columns that contain sensitive or unnecessary data.
Press Option + / to open the Tool Finder and search for any menu command.
Use your arrow keys to move between cells instead of clicking every time.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur where a specific menu item is if you forget a shortcut.

blocks.text: Managing your time and evaluation logs

Many evaluators track their time in a dedicated sheet. Set up columns for Date, Project Name, Task Count, and Time Spent. Use the =SUM() formula at the bottom of your time column to keep a running total. If you notice your sheet getting slow, check if you have exceeded the 20 million cell limit. Most evaluation logs stay well under this cap.

If you are struggling with a complex formula, ask Lazur to explain it. Hold ⌥ ⌘, point at the cell, and ask what the formula does. Lazur will read the logic out loud, helping you debug errors like #REF! or #NAME? without leaving your seat.

blocks.text: Common mistakes and how to fix them

One common issue is accidental data loss. Always use the Revision History to recover deleted entries. Go to File > Version History > See version history. You can restore your sheet to a previous state from minutes or hours ago. Another issue is permission errors. If you have multiple Google accounts, log out of all of them. Sign back into the one associated with your evaluation work to avoid access denied messages.

Use filters to keep your workspace clean. Select your header row and go to Data > Create a filter. This adds small icons to your column headers. You can click these to hide completed tasks or show only specific projects. This is much faster than scrolling through a long list of entries.

When you have thousands of rows, performance might dip. Try to keep your formatting simple. Avoid excessive use of conditional formatting across the entire sheet. If you need to analyze data, create a separate tab for your summary. Use a Pivot Table to group your tasks by project or date. This keeps your main input sheet light and responsive.

faq.question: Is there a native Google Sheets app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, Google Sheets is a web-based app. You can create a PWA shortcut in Chrome to make it act like a standalone app on your Mac.

faq.question: How do I speed up data entry in Sheets?
faq.answer: Use keyboard shortcuts like ⌘ + / to find tools, and use Lazur to dictate notes directly into cells.

faq.question: What should I do if my sheet is lagging?
faq.answer: Check for too many formulas or excessive conditional formatting. Consider moving historical data to a new sheet.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my Google Sheets files for me?
faq.answer: No, Lazur cannot click buttons or edit files. It can guide you through the steps, point at menu items, or dictate text for you.
